root_cause.text: Missing propagation of the SKBFL_SHARED_FRAG flag when moving frag descriptors between skbs, causing the destination skb to incorrectly report that it does not have shared pages, which leads to unsafe in-place writes that can corrupt read-only page-cache files.
root_cause.evidence: The CVE description states that helpers like __pskb_copy_fclone() and skb_shift() "fail to propagate the SKBFL_SHARED_FRAG bit in skb_shinfo()->flags when moving frags from source to destination," resulting in "the destination skb keeps a reference to the same externally-owned or page-cache-backed pages while reporting skb_has_shared_frag() as false." It further explains that this allows an unprivileged user to "write into the page cache of a root-owned read-only file via authencesn-ESN stray writes." The patch diff introduces lines such as `skb_shinfo(n)->flags |= skb_shinfo(skb)->flags & SKBFL_SHARED_FRAG` in the affected helpers to fix the omission.

intent_record.intent_summary: Propagate the SKBFL_SHARED_FRAG flag from the incoming skb to the GRO head and last skb to preserve correct shared fragment handling during GRO merging.
intent_record.what: Added two lines in skb_gro_receive() to set the SKBFL_SHARED_FRAG flag in shinfo->flags of the head skb (p) and the last skb (lp) by OR-ing the incoming skb's flags masked with SKBFL_SHARED_FRAG.
intent_record.how: When merging a new skb into a GRO session, the SKBFL_SHARED_FRAG flag from the incoming skb is now propagated to the head skb and the last skb (if different). This ensures that the shared fragment state is correctly maintained across merged skbs, affecting memory management and reference counts.

intent_record.intent_summary: Propagate the SKBFL_SHARED_FRAG flag from the incoming skb to the head skb when merging in skb_gro_receive_list to correctly track shared fragment state and prevent memory management issues.
intent_record.what: Added line sets the SKBFL_SHARED_FRAG flag in p's skb_shared_info->flags if it is set in skb's flags, using a bitwise OR operation.
intent_record.how: At runtime, this ensures that when merging an skb into a list via skb_gro_receive_list, the shared fragment flag from the incoming skb is propagated to the head skb, preserving correct semantics for fragment sharing and reference counting.

intent_record.intent_summary: Fix missing propagation of SKBFL_SHARED_FRAG flag when copying fragments in __pskb_copy_fclone.
intent_record.what: Added a line to propagate the SKBFL_SHARED_FRAG flag from the original skb's shared info to the copy's shared info after copying fragments.
intent_record.how: During fragment copying in __pskb_copy_fclone, the new skb now inherits the SKBFL_SHARED_FRAG flag from the original, ensuring that the flag correctly indicates shared fragment status.

intent_record.intent_summary: Propagate the SKBFL_SHARED_FRAG flag from source to target skb during fragment shift to maintain correct shared frag ownership.
intent_record.what: Added a line to propagate the SKBFL_SHARED_FRAG flag from the source skb's shared info to the target skb's shared info during skb_shift.
intent_record.how: This ensures that if the source skb's fragments are marked as shared, the target skb also gets that flag set, preventing premature freeing or refcounting errors after the fragment shift.

intent_record.intent_summary: Fix skb_segment to include frag_skb's shared frag flags when setting flags on the new segment.
intent_record.what: Modified the assignment of skb_shinfo(nskb)->flags in skb_segment to include skb_shinfo(frag_skb)->flags in the OR expression before AND with SKBFL_SHARED_FRAG.
intent_record.how: When segmenting a socket buffer, the new segment's shared fragment flags are now computed from both the head_skb and frag_skb, ensuring that any relevant flags from frag_skb are propagated to the new segment.

intent_record.intent_summary: Propagate the SKBFL_SHARED_FRAG flag during skb segmentation to fix a bug where shared fragment status was lost, preventing use-after-free.
intent_record.what: Added a line that copies the SKBFL_SHARED_FRAG flag from frag_skb's skb_shared_info flags to nskb's skb_shared_info flags using bitwise operations.
intent_record.how: During skb segmentation, the new skb (nskb) will now inherit the SKBFL_SHARED_FRAG flag from the original fragment skb (frag_skb), ensuring that shared fragment status is correctly preserved, which affects page reference counting and prevents premature freeing.

intent_record.intent_summary: Propagate SKBFL_SHARED_FRAG flag from source to destination skb when cloning fragments to fix missing flag handling for shared pages.
intent_record.what: Added line to propagate SKBFL_SHARED_FRAG flag from source skb to destination skb when cloning payload fragments in tcp_clone_payload.
intent_record.how: When cloning fragments, the destination skb now inherits the SKBFL_SHARED_FRAG flag if it was set in the source, ensuring correct tracking of shared fragment pages.

candidates.rationale: This statement adds frag data length to the last GRO skb (lp) but does not propagate the SKBFL_SHARED_FRAG flag, leaving the skb reporting that its pages are not shared even though they may be shared with the incoming skb.

When merging skbs in skb_gro_receive_list, this statement accounts for the truesize of the incoming skb (which includes shared frags) but fails to propagate the SKBFL_SHARED_FRAG flag to the head skb, allowing unsafe in-place writes.

During fragment copying in __pskb_copy_fclone, this statement takes a reference to the original fragment but does not copy the SKBFL_SHARED_FRAG flag to the new skb, causing the new skb to incorrectly indicate that its pages are not shared.
After shifting fragments from one skb to another, this statement updates the target skb's length but does not propagate the SKBFL_SHARED_FRAG flag, leading to missing shared fragment tracking.
This statement only propagates the SKBFL_SHARED_FRAG flag from head_skb, ignoring frag_skb which may also have the flag, thus failing to fully preserve shared fragment status during segmentation.
